title: Integrated valorization of waste cooking oil and spent Coccus nucifera biosorbent for biodiesel production
content:
Abstract

This study investigates the sustainable valorization of Coccus nucifera shell ash within a circular economy framework, addressing waste management and renewable energy production. Motivated by the need for eco-friendly solutions to dye pollution and biodiesel production, this research hypothesizes that Coccus nucifera shell ash can function as both an efficient adsorbent for methylene blue (MB) dye and a green catalyst for biodiesel synthesis. MB adsorption was evaluated under varying conditions, achieving a 98.93% removal rate with an adsorption capacity of 19.787 mg/g at pH 8. Calcined ash was then utilized as a heterogeneous catalyst, attaining a 92.08% biodiesel yield with a relative standard deviation of 1.028% from waste cooking oil (W.C.O.) at optimized conditions (adsorbent dosage: 0.375 g, contact time: 150 min, temperature: 65°C, MTOR: 18.5 mL) using the Taguchi method. Gray relational analysis identified temperature as the most critical factor. This study demonstrates an innovative dual-function approach, highlighting the potential of Coccus nucifera shell ash for integrated dye remediation and biodiesel production, aligning with sustainability goals.
